case: Oil States Energy Services, LLC v. Greene's Energy Group, LLC
summary: Inter partes review is constitutional. Sued for infringement, Greene's petitions for IPR; the Board holds the claims unpatentable; the Federal Circuit affirms without opinion under Rule 36; Oil States wins certiorari on the Article III / Seventh Amendment question. Exercises the PTAB -> CAFC link, the ipr-estopped flag and the Rule 36 path.

legs.context: U.S. Patent No. 6,179,053 (wellhead protection for fracking) issued to Oil States in 2001.

steps.event: Oil States sues Greene's for infringement in the E.D. Tex.
Near the close of discovery, Greene's petitions for IPR2014-00216 against claims 1 and 22 (exact date not found)
Oil States files a response opposing review
The Board decides institution (date not found)
Sur-reply: forced by the pack (see quirks)
Oil States moves to amend (the FWD denies the motion)
Preliminary guidance: forced by the pack (see quirks)
Oral hearing (not found in the sources read; route assumed)
Final written decision: claims 1 and 22 unpatentable as anticipated; motion to amend denied (Paper 53)
No rehearing or Director review in the sources read; straight to appeal (route assumed)
Oil States appeals to the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. § 141)
Entries of appearance and certificates of interest
Rule 36 judgment of affirmance without opinion, 639 F. App'x 639
Bill of costs (route assumed; the pack requires it)

gaps.event: Supreme Court affirms (argued 2017-11-27, decided 2018-04-24, 7-2): IPR adjudicates a public right and does not violate Article III or the Seventh Amendment
gaps.why: No pack models Supreme Court merits review; cert-granted is terminal.

deadlines.arithmetic: 37 C.F.R. § 90.3(a): 63 days. May 1 + 30 = May 31; + 30 = Jun 30 (60); + 3 = Jul 3 (63), a Friday, but the observed Independence Day holiday (July 4 fell on a Saturday); the next day that is not a weekend or holiday is Monday Jul 6.
deadlines.historical: Notice-of-appeal date not found; the appeal is No. 2015-1855. The op applies FRAP 26 (the CAFC instance's rule set); 37 C.F.R. § 90.3(c), which actually governs a PTAB notice, rolls forward the same way here.
Petition filed 2016-11-23, a month after the unextended date. An extension under Sup. Ct. R. 13.5 is the usual explanation, but none was found in the sources read.

quirks: The PTAB pack forces a patent-owner sur-reply and, after a motion to amend, Board preliminary guidance. Neither existed when this trial ran (2014-15): sur-replies arrived with the August 2018 Trial Practice Guide update and preliminary guidance with the 2019 motion-to-amend pilot.

The PTAB pack's own federal-circuit-window deadline (63 days) cannot be computed by the `deadlines` op: the pack's forum 'ptab' maps to no rule set (37 C.F.R. § 1.7 / § 90.3(c) are not implemented). The check above uses the CAFC instance's copy of the same deadline.
The CAFC pack tags cert-granted with outcome 'remand' even when the Court goes on to affirm.
The CAFC pack requires a bill-of-costs step before the certiorari window.
